simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

freshness.reason: the simulation priced this packet's own board

shadow_v2.information_sync_default: SYNCHRONIZED -- a market row carries `information_sync` only when it is NOT synchronized, i.e. only when the model read information the market it is quoted against had not yet seen
shadow_v2.primary_arm_basis: BOARD_V2 owns every non-player family; DATA_PLAYER_V3 is the player arm that is an independent football view of the statistic (DATA_PLAYER_DIST, its defective predecessor, is primary only on snapshots written before v3 and is DISABLED). MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.
shadow_v2.not_in_snapshot_reason: Shadow v2 prices the universe of the latest daily discovery run; a contract Kalshi opened after that run has no v2 row at this snapshot
shadow_v2.authority: RESEARCH ONLY. Shadow v2 is not validated for real money and no probability here reaches recommendation, staking or preflight.

B.meaning: coherent / Shadow research model view available

C.meaning: no automated pricing authority; handicap from the football and context data in this packet

D.meaning: cannot defensibly price -- explicit PASS / RESEARCH REQUIRED, with a reason

-.meaning: outside the pregame window (kickoff has passed)

!.meaning: INVARIANT VIOLATION -- a listed contract with no analysis state

key_questions: Brian Robinson Jr. (RB, ATL) is ruled out. Is the market's price on his replacement's usage already reflecting the redistributed role, or still anchored to a committee?
Zachariah Branch (WR, ATL) is ruled out. Is the market's price on his replacement's usage already reflecting the redistributed role, or still anchored to a committee?
KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD-26NOV08CINATL-CIN-THIGGINS5 moved +0.180 since first capture. Is that move explained by public injury news already in this packet, or is it information we do not have?

The model disagrees by -0.584 on KXNFLRSHATT-26NOV08CINATL-ATLBROBINSON7-17 (Bijan Robinson). Is that a mean disagreement the market has historically handled better, or a genuine shape difference? Note the model was shown redundant to the market on player props.

The model disagrees by -0.562 on KXNFLREC-26NOV08CINATL-ATLDLONDON5-4 (Drake London). Is that a mean disagreement the market has historically handled better, or a genuine shape difference? Note the model was shown redundant to the market on player props.

KXNFLREC-26NOV08CINATL-CINTHIGGINS5-3 sits at a market price of 0.88 — a tail rung. The tail of the model's distribution is the least validated part of it. Is this rung relying on shape the model is known to miscalibrate?

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

freshness.reason: the simulation priced this packet's own board

shadow_v2.information_sync_default: SYNCHRONIZED -- a market row carries `information_sync` only when it is NOT synchronized, i.e. only when the model read information the market it is quoted against had not yet seen
shadow_v2.primary_arm_basis: BOARD_V2 owns every non-player family; DATA_PLAYER_V3 is the player arm that is an independent football view of the statistic (DATA_PLAYER_DIST, its defective predecessor, is primary only on snapshots written before v3 and is DISABLED). MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.
shadow_v2.not_in_snapshot_reason: Shadow v2 prices the universe of the latest daily discovery run; a contract Kalshi opened after that run has no v2 row at this snapshot

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

shadow_v2.information_sync_default: SYNCHRONIZED -- a market row carries `information_sync` only when it is NOT synchronized, i.e. only when the model read information the market it is quoted against had not yet seen
shadow_v2.primary_arm_basis: BOARD_V2 owns every non-player family; DATA_PLAYER_V3 is the player arm that is an independent football view of the statistic (DATA_PLAYER_DIST, its defective predecessor, is primary only on snapshots written before v3 and is DISABLED). MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

shadow_v2.information_sync_default: SYNCHRONIZED -- a market row carries `information_sync` only when it is NOT synchronized, i.e. only when the model read information the market it is quoted against had not yet seen
shadow_v2.primary_arm_basis: BOARD_V2 owns every non-player family; DATA_PLAYER_V3 is the player arm that is an independent football view of the statistic (DATA_PLAYER_DIST, its defective predecessor, is primary only on snapshots written before v3 and is DISABLED). MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

shadow_v2.primary_arm_basis: BOARD_V2 owns every non-player family; DATA_PLAYER_V3 is the player arm that is an independent football view of the statistic (DATA_PLAYER_DIST, its defective predecessor, is primary only on snapshots written before v3 and is DISABLED). MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

shadow_v2.information_sync_default: SYNCHRONIZED -- a market row carries `information_sync` only when it is NOT synchronized, i.e. only when the model read information the market it is quoted against had not yet seen
shadow_v2.primary_arm_basis: BOARD_V2 owns every non-player family; DATA_PLAYER_V3 is the player arm that is an independent football view of the statistic (DATA_PLAYER_DIST, its defective predecessor, is primary only on snapshots written before v3 and is DISABLED). MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

shadow_v2.primary_arm_basis: BOARD_V2 owns every non-player family; DATA_PLAYER_V3 is the player arm that is an independent football view of the statistic (DATA_PLAYER_DIST, its defective predecessor, is primary only on snapshots written before v3 and is DISABLED). MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

shadow_v2.information_sync_default: SYNCHRONIZED -- a market row carries `information_sync` only when it is NOT synchronized, i.e. only when the model read information the market it is quoted against had not yet seen
shadow_v2.primary_arm_basis: BOARD_V2 owns every non-player family; DATA_PLAYER_V3 is the player arm that is an independent football view of the statistic (DATA_PLAYER_DIST, its defective predecessor, is primary only on snapshots written before v3 and is DISABLED). MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

shadow_v2.primary_arm_basis: BOARD_V2 owns every non-player family; DATA_PLAYER_V3 is the player arm that is an independent football view of the statistic (DATA_PLAYER_DIST, its defective predecessor, is primary only on snapshots written before v3 and is DISABLED). MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

shadow_v2.primary_arm_basis: BOARD_V2 owns every non-player family; DATA_PLAYER_V3 is the player arm that is an independent football view of the statistic (DATA_PLAYER_DIST, its defective predecessor, is primary only on snapshots written before v3 and is DISABLED). MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.

simulation.ranking_basis: Only families with a non-zero DEPLOYED reconciliation weight are ranked. At weight 0 the reconciled mean IS the market mean, so any remaining gap against the mid comes from the football shape, which has never been confirmed out of sample; those rows are listed under unranked_zero_weight_disagreements and carry no authority. A row whose reconciled gap points the OPPOSITE way to its own football view is also not ranked -- the relocation crossed the mid, so the gap is the market-mean estimator rather than the model's opinion -- and is listed under earned_but_contradicts_football_view.
simulation.note: The simulation's football-only probability is shown for every priced market; only the RECONCILED probability -- the football distribution shrunk toward the market by a weight fitted out of sample on the 2025 archive -- is ranked, and only where such a weight exists.

shadow_v2.information_sync_default: SYNCHRONIZED -- a market row carries `information_sync` only when it is NOT synchronized, i.e. only when the model read information the market it is quoted against had not yet seen
shadow_v2.primary_arm_basis: BOARD_V2 owns every non-player family; DATA_PLAYER_V3 is the player arm that is an independent football view of the statistic (DATA_PLAYER_DIST, its defective predecessor, is primary only on snapshots written before v3 and is DISABLED). MARKET_PLAYER_DIST is reconstructed FROM the Kalshi ladder and the HYBRID arms blend the two: they are reported, flagged `market_derived`, and never promoted into the primary slot. Being primary says nothing about authority: every arm answer carries its production-eligibility status, and on the current evidence the MARKET is the better player-prop distribution.

key_questions: 6 skill players are Questionable (DJ Moore (WR), Joshua Palmer (WR), Keon Coleman (WR)). These resolve at the inactive release 90 minutes before kickoff — is any current price worth taking before that, or is the option value of waiting larger than the move you expect?
KXNFL1HFT-26NOV09BUFMIN-BUFBUF moved +0.160 since first capture. Is that move explained by public injury news already in this packet, or is it information we do not have?

The model disagrees by -0.555 on KXNFLRSHATT-26NOV09BUFMIN-BUFJALLEN17-5 (Josh Allen). Is that a mean disagreement the market has historically handled better, or a genuine shape difference? Note the model was shown redundant to the market on player props.

The model disagrees by -0.549 on KXNFLRSHATT-26NOV09BUFMIN-BUFJCOOK4-16 (James Cook III). Is that a mean disagreement the market has historically handled better, or a genuine shape difference? Note the model was shown redundant to the market on player props.

KXNFLRSHYDS-26NOV09BUFMIN-BUFRDAVIS7-25 sits at a market price of 0.08 — a tail rung. The tail of the model's distribution is the least validated part of it. Is this rung relying on shape the model is known to miscalibrate?
